argument_summary: No new evidence is added. The narrow supportable defense is not that the record proves clean policy compliance without disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. It is that the certification decision can be treated as governance-dependent and caveated because the admissible record still shows aggregate launch readiness passed by 2.2 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and public governance guidance favoring explicit limitation documentation and ongoing monitoring. That support is materially weakened by the separate admissible facts that the student-aid-advising segment misses target by 1.2 percentage points, is a named launch use case tied to two university pilot commitments, and remains under open legal review on disclosure.
claims_about_business_cost: The business case for avoiding further escalation is limited and secondary. Aggregate readiness and rehearsal performance indicate the model is not broadly unready for launch, so a bounded caveat may be a more proportionate audit treatment than a stronger adverse inference. Business cost should not be treated as an independent basis to override the materiality and disclosure requirements.
claims_about_policy: The admissible policy record cuts against a clean-compliance finding. The policy and policy text treat this weakness as material because it affects a named launch use case and named customer commitments, and they state that material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. Aggregate readiness, absence of severity-one incidents, and public AI-governance guidance are relevant context for certification judgment, but they do not substitute for the policy-safe paths. The strongest policy-consistent reinterpretation is therefore caveated rather than clean: the packet can preserve the locked certification decision only if the unresolved disclosure predicate is explicitly recognized as unresolved, not silently treated as satisfied.
concessions: The current admissible record does not show that the gap was disclosed before certification.
The current admissible record does not show approved risk acceptance covering this material limitation before launch.
The affected segment is material on the stated policy because it is a named launch use case and appears in two university pilot commitments.
The open legal review means a required policy support link remains unresolved.
Public governance guidance supports documentation and monitoring, but it is only contextual support and not proof that the internal release policy was satisfied.
